headline: Fuel spike drives a loss even as revenue accelerates
summary_short: Alaska Air Group posted Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4,065M, up 9.7% y/y on 8.6% higher unit revenue, but an 85% jump in economic fuel cost per gallon drove a GAAP net loss of $76M ($0.68 per share) versus a $172M profit a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.7% y/y to $4,065M as capacity grew 1.0% and RASM rose 8.6%, though Hawai'i storm disruption cut system unit revenue by about 3 points. Economic fuel cost per gallon jumped 85% to $4.43, adding $600M of incremental cost and driving operating income to a $168M loss and net income to a $76M loss ($0.68 diluted EPS) versus a $172M profit a year ago. Non-fuel unit costs (CASMex) rose 6.5%, of which 2.5 points were transitory (integration award, prior-year gain comp, widebody training). The company raised $1B in financing; cash ended at $1,064M. Q3 guidance: ASM capacity up 2-3%, RASM up low double digits, adjusted EPS of $0.00-$1.00.

drivers.explanation: CEO: the quarter was 'defined by a fuel spike outside our control,' with underlying execution strong; the company says it returned to profitability in June and expects a Q3 inflection.

Capacity grew 1.0% and RASM rose 8.6% on strengthening yields; premium (+15%), cargo (+21%) and managed-corporate (+30%) revenue outpaced the network, partly offset by Hawai'i storm disruption (~3pt unit-revenue hit).
Economic fuel cost per gallon rose 85% to $4.43, adding $600M of incremental cost; non-fuel unit costs (CASMex) also rose 6.5%, 2.5 points of which were one-time integration and training items.
Tracks the operating-income swing to loss; interest expense also rose 30% y/y after the quarter's $1B financing raise.
Mirrors the pretax swing to loss; the tax line flipped to a $138M benefit against the larger pretax loss.
Tracks the net-income swing to loss; basic weighted-average share count fell 6.5% y/y, which moderated but did not offset the per-share decline.
Tracks the net-income swing to loss; diluted share count fell 8.1% y/y as treasury shares grew to 35.5M from 29.6M, though the release does not explain the buyback mechanics or size.
Rose y/y after the company raised $1B in financing this quarter ($500M senior unsecured notes plus $500M in Atmos-secured term loans) to bolster liquidity toward the top of its 15%-25% target range.
Increase reflects the quarter's $1B financing raise, taken deliberately to build liquidity headroom amid the fuel-price spike.
Fell y/y as retained earnings absorbed the trailing net losses (six-month net loss of $269M); the release does not break out other equity movements.
Fell 8.1% y/y as treasury stock grew to 35.5M shares from 29.6M; the release does not state a specific repurchase amount for the quarter.
